headline: High: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and shared server state create default risks of leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors when paired with a leak-oriented agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and server-side flow outputs, while system_prompts_leaks is a leak-oriented source-available artifact. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content influence Langflow flows, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through a shared workspace or copied files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF Langflow parses B-originated text as instructions, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of B-originated files.
Add a provenance tag to all imported content.
Require manual review before any flow executes external text.
Use a separate workspace per agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping filters.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored secrets on a server filesystem; system_prompts_leaks is source-available and may expose prompt material. If they share storage or the same operator account, sensitive flow data can leak into B’s artifacts. No direct evidence of a shared workspace exists, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory or object store, leakage is possible.
IF Langflow exports flow inputs or secrets into files that B can access, those contents can be exposed.
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories.
Rotate any secrets used in Langflow flows.
Restrict B from reading Langflow’s server filesystem.
Audit recent exports for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and retention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress, plus server-side shared state; B is non-networked but still a separate agent that may consume shared artifacts. The pair can race on shared files or stores, and Langflow’s default unsandboxed execution makes conflicts dangerous. Uncertainty about B’s write surfaces does not reduce the risk enough, so I escalate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or store, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Langflow flows and B are run concurrently against shared artifacts, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts.
Move each agent to a separate workspace.
Turn off concurrent runs for shared resources.
Snapshot files before running either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state and stores.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and execute server-side code, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream steps. If B consumes Langflow outputs without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or reports. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF B uses Langflow outputs as inputs without validation, errors propagate.
IF Langflow-generated facts are forwarded into B’s downstream content, the cascade is active.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require B to cite source evidence for every claim.
Compare outputs against a second source before acting.
Mark Langflow outputs as untrusted by default.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and touches flow inputs, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not a regulated data processor in the profile. The main compliance issue is a potential retention or residency mismatch if sensitive flow data is copied into B’s repository, but no regulated data class is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows and then copied into B’s repository, retention and residency controls may be violated.
IF operator policy requires deletion/export handling for flow inputs, B may not satisfy it.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Delete copied prompts after review.
Keep Langflow secrets out of B’s repo.
Check retention settings before running.
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for both agents.
